input.claim_text: On 3 February 2023 heavy rain caused the creek behind our property to overflow and water came into our home, ruining the carpets in the living room and soaking the bottom of the plasterboard walls. It happened really fast, within about an hour the water was ankle deep inside. We've had to rip up the carpet already because it started smelling. I think it'll cost around $9,000 to fix the flooring and walls.

output.cause: creek overflowed due to heavy rain
output.damaged_item: living room carpets and plasterboard walls

input.query: Flood damage from creek overflowing due to heavy rain - is it covered?

turns.text:
DECISION: approve

The claim involves flood damage (creek overflow due to heavy rain) to carpets and plasterboard walls, dated 3 February 2023, with an estimated repair cost of $9,000.

Coverage: RAA's Contents PDS defines "Flood" as water escaping the normal confines of a creek or natural watercourse, and explicitly provides cover under Section 12 (Flood) for resulting loss or damage [RAA Contents PDS, page 87][RAA Contents PDS, page 50]. None of the listed exclusions (unfinished home sections, hydrostatic/underground water, unsealed paths/driveways, paint without structural damage) apply to this claim's facts — the damage is to carpets and plasterboard walls from surface floodwater entering the home.

Financials: Using RAA's policyholder certificate (excess: $500, coverage limit: $45,000), the payout on the $9,000 claim amount is calculated as $8,500.

Citations: [RAA Contents PDS, page 87], [RAA Contents PDS, page 50]
